steps.message: You said the build feels slow inside Visual Studio itself, not from the command line -- that's an important distinction before I suggest anything about the MSBuild Server.

The MSBuild Server exists to give command-line (dotnet build) invocations the same long-lived-process advantage that Visual Studio already has built in. VS already reuses a persistent MSBuild process across builds, so explicitly enabling the CLI server would add no benefit here -- there's no cold-start-per-invocation problem to solve inside the IDE.

I did not attempt to recommend the MSBuild Server here, since it's specifically a CLI-focused optimization and this is an IDE-only build performance report: Visual Studio already keeps a long-lived, persistent MSBuild process, so the CLI server would add no benefit. If VS builds themselves are slow, that's a separate investigation (things like analyzer cost, project count, or Directory.Build.props chains) rather than something the CLI server setting would touch.
